summary: A private verification clone that differs from its commit now names the paths. Git can leave a tracked file out of a checkout that still exits 0, and the clone then differs from its commit before any command ran, yet `environment --verb up` refused with only "runtime checkout changed; only teardown is allowed before a new verification session" and a command run recorded only `candidate_intact` false, which read as a file the command had changed. The runtime refusal now reads "runtime checkout changed (missing <path>); ...", a QA command run, a pre-handoff regression run or a runtime event that is not intact records the paths as `checkout_difference`, and a freeze that such a pre-handoff run refuses names them as well. A path the checkout lacks is marked missing, any other is marked changed, and at most five are named before a count of the rest. What each refusal allows is unchanged.
